root_cause.text: In MPTCP `__mptcp_retrans()`, the reinjection/retransmission path was allowed to run while `msk->fallback_lock` was held during the MP_FAIL-to-infinite-map fallback critical section, leading to recursive re-entry into fallback code (`__mptcp_try_fallback`) and self-deadlock on the same lock.
root_cause.evidence: The lockdep trace shows `__mptcp_retrans` already holding `&msk->fallback_lock` before `__mptcp_try_fallback` tries to acquire it again, and the patch fixes this by skipping retransmission when fallback is active or when `!msk->allow_subflows` (“we can't retrans even when an infinite fallback is in progress”).

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent MPTCP retransmission from proceeding when fallback is active or new subflows are disallowed during infinite fallback.
intent_record.what: The change updates the retransmission path in __mptcp_retrans() by extending the condition guarded by msk->fallback_lock: the existing check of __mptcp_check_fallback(msk) is changed to also test !msk->allow_subflows, and the surrounding comment is expanded to state that retransmission must not proceed while an infinite fallback is in progress because new subflows are disallowed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, retransmission through this path will now be skipped not only when fallback is already active, but also when subflow creation is disabled via allow_subflows being false. This prevents attempting retransmission logic that depends on opening or using additional subflows during an infinite fallback state.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent MPTCP retransmission from proceeding when fallback is active or new subflows are disallowed during infinite fallback.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly prevents the retransmission/reinjection path from running during fallback/infinite-map conditions, which is the core scenario that caused recursive fallback re-entry and self-deadlock while fallback_lock was held.

candidates.rationale: This acquires fallback_lock before entering the retransmission decision/xmit path. The root cause is that retransmission was allowed to proceed while this lock was held, enabling recursive re-entry into fallback handling and causing self-deadlock on the same lock.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement acquires msk->fallback_lock before entering the retransmission/reinjection path in __mptcp_retrans(). Because the code then allowed retransmission handling to proceed while the lock was held, fallback logic could be re-entered recursively via __mptcp_try_fallback(), causing self-deadlock on the same lock during the MP_FAIL infinite-map fallback critical section.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff directly shows the relevant logic in `__mptcp_retrans()` and includes the added fallback serialization that addresses the root cause. In this version, retransmission now executes under `msk->fallback_lock`: `spin_lock_bh(&msk->fallback_lock);` followed by `if (__mptcp_check_fallback(msk)) { spin_unlock_bh(&msk->fallback_lock); release_sock(ssk); return; }`, then the retransmission loop, and finally `spin_unlock_bh(&msk->fallback_lock);`. The comment explicitly states the intent: `make the whole retrans decision, xmit, disallow fallback atomic`. This prevents the reinjection/retransmission path from running concurrently with fallback state transitions and avoids the recursive fallback re-entry/self-deadlock described in the root cause. The function also initializes `info` as `struct mptcp_sendmsg_info info = { .data_lock_held = true, };`, but the key fix is the lock-and-check around the retransmission path. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version, and the fix is present.
